title: Fairness in Language Models Beyond English: Gaps and Challenges

bias_targets.methodology: The paper surveys methodologies including intrinsic metrics (e.g., WEAT, SEAT, StereoSet) applied to multilingual embeddings, and extrinsic metrics on downstream tasks like text classification and masked language modeling. It specifically reviews how these metrics evaluate grammatical, referential, and lexical gender across different languages.

The paper reviews methodologies that evaluate cultural context retention in models, looking at cross-lingual transfer, culturally-sensitive datasets, and the impact of localized sociolinguistic variables, taboos, and dialects in language representation.

The survey evaluates the measurement of racial and ethnic bias through extrinsic evaluation benchmarks, particularly in multilingual text classification and hate speech detection datasets annotated with author demographic attributes.
Reviewed through multilingual text classification benchmarks and datasets that incorporate age as a demographic variable to assess fairness in downstream tasks.

The paper discusses the conceptual need to evaluate localized hierarchical prejudices, such as caste in India and Nepal, highlighting gaps in current methodologies and the necessity of region-specific demographic evaluation.
